mainTopic: Which favors count as forbidden benefit for someone barred by vow from his friend's food or benefit (המודר הנאה מחבירו)
overview: The משנה said that someone who vowed off his friend's food may not borrow food-making tools like a sieve or an oven. The גמרא asks how tools can be forbidden when the vow was only about food. ריש לקיש says the vow was 'benefit of your food,' and רבא widens it to 'benefit that leads to your food.' רב פפא adds that a sack, a donkey or a basket for carrying produce also count. He then asks about less direct help: a horse to ride, a ring to be seen with, and walking across the friend's land. A proof from the משנה, which allows lending rings, is rejected, so the ring question stays unanswered. The next משנה forbids even non-food items where people usually rent them out. From this, the גמרא infers that food tools are forbidden even where people lend them for free, and רב אדא בר אהבה says this follows רבי אליעזר. A further משנה allows the friend to pay the barred person's half-shekel and debt and return his lost item. The גמרא explains that paying a debt is just 'chasing away a lion.' רב הושעיא begins to name the תנא behind this, and his answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: But he only vowed off food
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the משנה: the person vowed off food, so why are food-making tools forbidden to him?
steps.simpleTranslation: But he vowed off food! (A sieve or an oven is not food.)
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the משנה's ruling that a person who vowed off his friend's food may not borrow his tools. Tools are not food, so the ruling seems too strict.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A נדר only forbids what the person actually said. He said 'food,' and a sieve, millstone or oven is not something you eat. So the משנה seems to forbid more than the vow covered.

phrases.english: But he vowed from food!
phrases.notes: This goes back to the משנה, which forbade lending him a sieve, millstone or oven. Those aren't food.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the משנה's list of forbidden items
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that someone who vowed off food may not borrow food-making tools
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The vow covered only food, and the tools are not food, so they should be permitted.

steps.title: The vow said 'benefit of your food'
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש answers that the משנה is talking about someone who vowed off any benefit connected to the friend's food.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן לקיש said: The case is where he said, 'Benefit from your food is forbidden to me.'
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש solves the problem by changing how we picture the vow. The person did not just say 'your food.' He said 'benefit from your food.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: By adding the word הנאה (benefit), the vow becomes wider than just eating. It now covers benefits that come from the food, and that might explain why more than eating is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: ריש לקיש, an אמורא of ארץ ישראל
in a case where he says

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said:
Where he says: 'Benefit of your food is forbidden to me.'

steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the wording of the vow
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The vow covered only eating the food itself.
steps.terutzMaskana: The vow covered any benefit from the friend's food.

steps.title: That wording covers only direct use of the food
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that 'benefit of your food' would only forbid using the food itself in some way, such as chewing wheat to put on a wound. It would not forbid tools.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say it means only that he may not chew wheat kernels and put them on his wound!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says ריש לקיש's answer is not enough. 'Benefit of your food' sounds like a benefit taken from the food itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Chewing the friend's wheat and using it as a bandage is a benefit from his food that is not eating. That is a good example of what 'benefit of your food' adds. A sieve or an oven is still not the food itself, so the problem from step 1 returns.

phrases.english: Say that he may not chew wheat kernels
and put them on his wound!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימָא שֶׁלֹּא יִלְעוֹס חִיטִּין וְיִתֵּן עַל מַכָּתוֹ
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's reading 'benefit of your food'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That wording only stretches to non-eating uses of the food itself, like a bandage. It does not reach tools used to prepare food.

steps.title: The vow said 'benefit that leads to your food'
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that the vow was worded 'benefit that leads to your food,' which includes the tools that prepare it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The case is where he said, 'Benefit that leads to your food is forbidden to me.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a wider wording of the vow that fits the משנה. The vow covers anything that helps bring about the friend's food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the words 'that leads to,' the vow is no longer limited to the food itself. A sieve, a millstone or an oven helps make food, so all of them are now forbidden. This finally explains the משנה.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's case is a vow worded 'benefit that leads to your food,' so anything that helps produce the friend's food is forbidden.

phrases.english: Rava said:
Where he says: 'Benefit that leads to your food is forbidden to me.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא בְּאוֹמֵר הֲנָאָה הַמְּבִיאָה לִידֵי מַאֲכָלְךָ עָלַי
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The vow covered only benefits from the food itself.
steps.terutzMaskana: The vow covered anything that leads to the food, including tools for preparing it.

steps.title: Sack, donkey and basket all lead to food
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא rules that a sack, a donkey or even a simple basket used to bring produce counts as 'benefit that leads to food.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: A sack to bring produce, a donkey to carry produce, even just a basket, all count as benefit that leads to food.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא applies רבא's wording to more cases. Anything used to carry food home counts too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה listed tools that prepare food. רב פפא adds that tools for transporting food also count. Even a cheap item like a plain basket is included.

keyTerms.meaning: a בבלי אמורא, student of רבא

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
A sack to bring produce,
and a donkey to bring produce on it,
and even just a basket,
it is benefit that leads to food.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא שַׂק לְהָבִיא פֵּירוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies רבא's wording to more examples
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Borrowing items used to carry food, such as a sack, a donkey or a basket, is forbidden under a vow of 'benefit that leads to your food.'

steps.title: What about a horse, a ring, or a shortcut?
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא asks about items that lead to food only indirectly: a horse to ride, a ring to be seen wearing, and crossing the friend's land.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא asked: A horse to ride on, or a ring to be seen wearing, what is the law? Crossing over and walking through his land, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא asks where the line is. These benefits only connect to food in a roundabout way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A sack carries food directly. A horse or a fancy ring might help only indirectly, for example by making the person look important so he gets served better at a meal. A shortcut across the friend's land gets him home to eat sooner. The question is whether such distant links still count as 'leading to food.'

keyTerms.meaning: to be seen with it (to show it off)

phrases.english: Rav Pappa asked:
A horse to ride on
and a ring to be seen with, what is the law?
Cutting across and walking on his land, what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from clear cases to unclear, indirect ones
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does an indirect benefit (horse, ring to be seen with, shortcut over land) count as 'benefit that leads to food'?

steps.title: Proof attempt from the משנה: rings may be lent
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries to answer the ring question from the משנה, which lets him borrow clothing and rings. That would only be worth saying if it means rings worn to be seen.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: 'But he may lend him a shirt, a cloak, nose rings and finger rings.' What is the case? If it means not to be seen with them, is that even worth saying? So doesn't it mean even to be seen with them, and still the משנה says he may lend them!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the משנה as a possible answer to רב פפא's ring question. It argues that the משנה must be talking about wearing the rings to show off.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the rings were not worn to be seen, there is no link to food at all, so the משנה would be telling us something obvious. A משנה doesn't teach something that obvious, so it must mean even rings worn to be seen. Since it still allows lending them, this would show that a ring to be seen with is not 'benefit that leads to food.'

keyTerms.meaning: come and hear (a proof is coming)
what is the case? / how do we picture it?
does it need to be said? (it's obvious)

steps.confusionAlert: This is only a proof attempt. The next step rejects it, so don't treat it as the final answer.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
But he may lend him a shirt and a cloak,
nose rings and finger rings.
What is the case?
If you say it's not to be seen with them,
does that need to be said?
Rather, isn't it even to be seen with them,
and yet it teaches 'he may lend it to him'!

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע אֲבָל מַשְׁאִיל לוֹ חָלוּק וְטַלִּית נְזָמִים וְטַבָּעוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to answer רב פפא's question from step 6
steps.raayaObject: רב פפא's question about a ring worn to be seen
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה permitting him to borrow clothing, nose rings and finger rings, read as covering rings worn to be seen, since otherwise the ruling would be obvious

steps.title: The ring proof is rejected
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back on the proof from step 7. The משנה may mean a ring that is not worn to be seen. It only said 'he may lend him' to match the wording of the first clause.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Really, the משנה means borrowing the ring not in order to be seen with it. And since the first part of the משנה said 'he may not lend him,' the last part was worded 'he may lend him.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the attempt to answer רב פפא's ring question from the משנה. So the question stays open.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 7 the proof was that the permission to lend rings only adds something if it means rings worn to be seen. The rejection says the משנה could be talking about a plain ring, which is obviously allowed. The משנה wrote 'he may lend him' only to balance the earlier phrase 'he may not lend him.'
steps.confusionAlert: 'Since the first part said X, it said Y' does not teach a new law. It means the wording was chosen for style, so you cannot learn a new law from it.
steps.whatToRemember: רב פפא's question about a ring worn to be seen is not answered by the משנה.

phrases.english: No, really it means not in order to be seen,
phrases.notes: He means the משנה is talking about borrowing a ring just to use it, not to show it off.

phrases.english: and since the first part teaches 'he may not lend him,'
it taught the last part as 'he may lend him.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof offered in step 7
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof is rejected. רב פפא's question stays unresolved.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה's permission can be read as being about a plain ring. Its wording comes from matching the first clause, not from teaching a new law.

steps.title: Non-food items are forbidden where people rent them
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה: an item not used for food is forbidden to borrow from the other person in a place where such items are normally rented out.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Any item that is not used to prepare food is forbidden in a place where people rent out items like it.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds a limit to the earlier permission to lend non-food items. Where such items are normally rented, borrowing one for free counts as forbidden benefit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, items like clothing and rings were allowed because they are not 'leading to food.' But if people usually pay rent for such an item, borrowing it free saves him money. He could use that money to buy food, so it becomes forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Food preparation (literally, food for a person)
Items like them, of that kind

phrases.english: משנה: And any item
that one does not use to prepare food,
in a place where people rent out items like it, it is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכׇל דָּבָר שֶׁאֵין עוֹשִׂין בּוֹ אוֹכֶל נֶפֶשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה with a new rule about non-food items
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A non-food item is forbidden to borrow where such items are usually rented out.

steps.title: Food tools are forbidden even where they are not rented
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא infers that the first clause (food tools) applies even where people do not rent those tools.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: By inference, the first clause applies even where people do not rent such items out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws an inference from the wording of the משנה. This sets up the next question about which תנא holds this view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only added the condition 'where people rent them' for non-food items. So food tools like a sieve must be forbidden even where people normally lend them for free. That is a strict position, and the גמרא will want to know whose view it is.

phrases.english: גמרא: By inference, the first clause applies
phrases.notes: The first clause is the one about food tools like a sieve or an oven.

phrases.english: even where people do not rent such items out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference from the משנה in step 9
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Food tools are forbidden even in a place where they are usually lent for free.

steps.title: Who is the author of this משנה?
steps.stepSummary: Since the inferred rule is strict, the גמרא asks which תנא taught it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who is the תנא of this משנה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whose opinion the משנה follows. It is setting up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Something people usually give for free is still counted here as forbidden benefit. Not every תנא would agree with that, so the גמרא looks for the source of the view.

keyTerms.meaning: Who is the תנא (author of this teaching)?

phrases.english: Who is the תנא?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the author of the strict rule inferred in step 10
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא forbids even benefits that are usually given for free

steps.title: It is רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה answers that this משנה follows רבי אליעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר אהבה said: It is רבי אליעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אדא בר אהבה identifies the author of the משנה as רבי אליעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר holds that even small things a person would normally let go of for free are forbidden to someone who is barred from benefit by a vow. That fits a משנה that forbids food tools even where they are lent at no cost.

keyTerms.meaning: The תנא whose strict view this משנה follows
The אמורא who answers the question

steps.whatToRemember: This משנה forbids even benefits usually given for free. It follows רבי אליעזר's strict view.

phrases.english: רב אדא בר אהבה said:
It is רבי אליעזר.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר הִיא
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה follows רבי אליעזר, who forbids even benefits normally given for free.

steps.title: Favors he may still do: shekel, debt, lost item
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה: the other person may pay the barred person's half-shekel, repay his debt, and return his lost item. Where people take payment for returning lost items, that benefit goes to הקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If someone is forbidden by vow to benefit from his friend, the friend may give the half-shekel for him, pay his debt, and return his lost item to him. In a place where people take payment for returning a lost item, the value of that benefit should go to הקדש.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה lists actions the friend may do even though the barred person may not benefit from him. It adds that if returning lost items is usually paid for, that benefit must be given to הקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Paying the shekel and the debt only removes an obligation and does not hand him anything directly, so it is allowed. Returning a lost item is a מצוה, so it is allowed too. But where people normally get paid for it, there is extra benefit, and that value goes to הקדש instead of to him.

keyTerms.meaning: One forbidden by vow to benefit
His half-shekel (yearly gift to the מקדש)

phrases.english: משנה: One forbidden by vow to benefit from his friend:
the friend may give his half-shekel for him
and pay off his debt,
and return his lost item to him.
In a place where people take payment for it,
phrases.notes: 'For it' means for returning a lost item.

phrases.english: the benefit should fall to הקדש.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַמּוּדָּר הֲנָאָה מֵחֲבֵירוֹ, שׁוֹקֵל לוֹ אֶת שִׁקְלוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה about indirect favors
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The friend may pay the barred person's shekel and debt and return his lost item. Where returning is usually paid for, the value of that benefit goes to הקדש.

steps.title: Paying a debt is like chasing away a lion
steps.stepSummary: From the משנה's rule that the other person may pay the barred person's debts, the גמרא learns that this only removes a danger and is not counted as giving benefit, so it is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: It seems that paying his debt is just chasing a lion away from him, and so it is allowed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins discussing the משנה by drawing a lesson from it. Paying someone's debt is like chasing a lion away from him. It removes a danger but gives him nothing new, so it is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה allowed paying the barred person's half-shekel and his debt, even though he is forbidden to benefit from the payer. The גמרא explains why. The payer does not hand the barred person anything. He only stops the creditor from bothering him, which is preventing harm, not giving benefit.

keyTerms.meaning: It seems / so we see: an inference drawn from the text
Chasing away a lion: removing a danger, not giving a gift

steps.confusionAlert: The payer is not giving the barred person money. He pays the creditor, and that only removes the creditor's pressure from the barred person.
steps.whyThisMatters: This idea sets up the question of which תנא holds that removing harm is not counted as benefit.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Apparently, [paying his debt] is chasing away a lion
phrases.notes: The lion stands for the creditor, so paying the debt makes the danger go away.

phrases.english: merely, and it is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the reason behind the משנה quoted in step 13
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Paying someone's debt only removes harm, like chasing away a lion, and is not forbidden benefit.

steps.title: Which תנא holds this view?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא holds that removing harm is not counted as benefit.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who is the תנא who taught this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which sage holds the view that paying a debt only chases away a lion. This question sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Not every sage agrees that removing harm is not counted as benefit. So the גמרא wants to know whose opinion the משנה follows.

keyTerms.meaning: A sage of the משנה period

phrases.english: Who is the tanna?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks whose opinion the inference in step 14 follows
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The identity of the תנא who holds that chasing away a lion is not counted as benefit

steps.title: רב הושעיא begins to answer
steps.stepSummary: רב הושעיא starts to identify the תנא. His answer continues in the next part of the text.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הושעיא begins answering which תנא this is. Only his opening word appears here, and the rest of his answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'This' points to the view in the משנה. רב הושעיא is about to say whose opinion it is.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who answers the question

phrases.english: Rav Hoshaya said: This

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the answer to the question in step 15
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The answer begins here ("This...") and is finished in the following text.
